name: BytePort
observation_method: Sequential connected-GitHub inventory and bounded default-history/source reads; selected fields transcribed, not a raw API export.
sampled_commit_scope: Latest default-history item returned at this repository read; not all branches or local state and not an atomic end-of-audit head.
movement: Two recent changes report removal of duplicate/conflicting global logger initialization in the Tauri application.
concerns: A logger fix is useful but is not a measured clean launch or a deployment journey.
Trace/log semantics can change when one logging layer is removed.

next_actions.title: Verify native launch and logging
next_actions.work: Run the actual packaged app from a clean profile outside the repository in debug/release where supported; test single initialization and usable diagnostic output.
next_actions.acceptance: No initialization panic, no duplicated/missing required logs, no secret exposure.

next_actions.title: Close one deployment path
next_actions.work: Connect a real permitted repository, build, provision, observe health/logs, update and roll back on one supported target.
next_actions.acceptance: A real service responds; failed provisioning and failed updates leave known recoverable state.

next_actions.title: Exercise current shared dependencies
next_actions.work: Coordinate runtime/manifest packages with PhenoShared and test cache-isolated source resolution and actual consumer behavior.
next_actions.acceptance: No reliance on a deleted path, warm Cargo cache or adjacent developer checkout; contract-compatible migration evidence.

ecosystem_contract: BytePort owns the deployment experience, not a new copy of the runtime foundation. Runtime capabilities must be negotiated and verified.
parent_acceptance: An installed client completes repository-to-service and recovery on a supported target.
scope_missing: actual chat receipts and read acknowledgement
